title: Two companies burn cash to win. Who actually wins?
hook: Two companies burn cash for years to win a market. Who actually wins? Usually nobody.

scenes.say: Two companies burn cash for years to win a market. Who actually wins? Usually nobody.
A war of attrition: both sides pay every day. Whoever lasts longer takes the prize.
Code runs {contests} contests over a prize worth {prize}, each side paying one per round.
scenes.note: Simulation: equilibrium quitting rate = cost / prize

scenes.say: On average, both sides together spend {avg_paid}. Basically the whole prize.
In {over_prize} of fights, they burn more than the prize is worth.
Before joining a war of attrition, add up what both sides will pay, not just the prize.

takeaway: Before joining a war of attrition, add up what both sides will pay, not just the prize.
